texts.text: <This place... looks like some kind of store...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: What exactly are they selling here? No, actually, why's anything being sold here in the first place?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I mean, it's a department store~
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Grand Magasin... A department store is, by nature, a place where a myriad little squares crowd upon one another in pursuit of profit.
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: I suppose we'll have to look around if we want to learn anything more in detai—
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Wha? What was that?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: What is that?!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: I don't know, but whatever it is, something huge...
texts.speaker: Gregor

texts.text: ... has plummeted from above.
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: That was close. We would have sustained a severe impact... had we moved a few steps closer to the side.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: It appears to be... a huge mass of human bodies tangled together, though the remains are far too severely mutilated to discern any individual forms.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: A big one dropped. Might be plenty worth salvaging this time. Hope the customers were heavy eyeball-spenders.
texts.speaker: Desperate Customer

texts.text: Damn it, I'm out of empty bottles! Hey, you borrowed three from me last season. When are you going to pay me back?!
texts.speaker: Destitute Customer

texts.text: Fuck off! This season's new drop is all... all mine. No one else's!
texts.speaker: Impatient Customer

texts.text: The pile that fell from the sky turns out to be corpses, mangled beyond all recognition. A curious golden glow, bright like sunlight, winks through the gaps between the bodies.
The people I assume to be the "customers" mentioned in the announcement are desperately scrambling among the corpses, snatching up whatever they could find.
Might we rest our steps awhile?
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: <Why, do you see anything up ahead?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That remains a subject to be discussed...
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: Yi Sang continued, clenching and unclenching his hand as he regarded us.
I have been set upon by this odd sensation... that which could not be a lone ideation of mine. This is the subject I wished to discuss with you.
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: I mean... Yeah, it's kinda hard to ignore. We've all grown weaker, like what happened to us when we first entered into that contract with Dante.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: ... This is likely not a permanent phenomenon. It is probable that the deterioration of your physical prowess is owed to the unique characteristic of the Grand Magasin Sisyphe.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: An issue with the very space of this place?
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: Correct. Entering Sisyphe through indirect means, such as the Suicide Vending Machine, does not change the fact that we have entered another state of existence as "customers" of the department store. Ergo, our bodies as we perceive them in the phenomenal sense must have been reconstructed according to the rules of this place, which involves the Shadowed and the Symbolic—
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: H-hold on!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: So you're basically sayin' that this place is to blame for making us weaker, and we're gonna get back to normal once we're out, am I right?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: ... Yes.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Hmm~ Then rather than waiting for more explanation or brainstorming for ways to get stronger...
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Best we find Meur and get out of this place, chop-chop.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Happy to have a consensus for once. Our highest priority at the moment is locating Meursault; we best table any intelligence pertaining to this phenomenon until that primary objective is accomplished.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: And if we run into fights? Any plans for that?
texts.speaker: Gregor

texts.text: *puff* Killing a W.C. or two won't be a problem even if we've become C.W.
texts.speaker: Ryōshū

texts.text: Killing a wandering customer or two won't be a problem even if we've become confused wimps, she says...
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <You know what, let's just go find Meursault like Rodya said.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Surprise, surprise...
... Who are you?
texts.speaker: Gregor

texts.text: You people are awfully lucky, aren't you?
Look at that gory mess! Must've fallen from the sixth floor, give or take. This pile'll make this spot famous as a prime drop zone for a while.
... Might you be talking to us?
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: What took you so long? I've been anxiously waiting for you 'round the clock!
For us? Why the hell would you...?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: In any case, aren't those... human bodies that just fell from above...? And what're those people even scavenging...?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Human, she says! Oh, you're positively whimsical, aren't you? Those were customers.
As for the scavengers, they heard a thud, so they've gathered up to try to get anything they can. Life's pretty rough in here, you know.
She's gone.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Let's quickly find Meursault and figure out how to get out of this place...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Should we... keep movin' for now? Straight ahead?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Executive Manager. I recommend returning to the restroom to regroup and reorganize.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: I... assent to Young Rodya's counsel. Let us set forth with all haste, forsooth...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <Yi Sang almost got hurt just now. And I think Sinclair needs a moment to collect himself.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Let's do as Outis said. Regroup in the restroom, take a breather, then head out.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Thank you, Manager...
texts.speaker: Sinclair

texts.text: <color=#916e46>Your attention, please. The Stripe Season has officially ended. We are pleased to inform you that Houndstooth is the new trend.</color>

What?! No! I flayed so much skin off my thighs to make those stripe patterns... and it was all for nothing?! I only just got the horizontal lines all the way up to my chin. They can't change the trend now!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: I have to fill the new-arrivals displays! Need a plan, need a plan... Maybe tear what's there into a checkered pattern? I can't let those go to clearance!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: <... Pretty hectic, huh...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <color=#515aee>Let me... lay my hands on you awhile.</color>
<color=#515aee>Every voyage... requires some touch... before it begins.</color>
<Meursault! So this is the place I saw... What are you doing here?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... I entered the Grand Magasin, proceeded onward, and arrived at this shop.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What the heck, Meur! Ya could at least pretend to be surprised to see us. We came to save ya!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: As far as I'm aware, entry to Sisyphe is beyond ordinary means.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: If you were not brought here via the Sisyphe Penalty, then you must have taken another, unknown route.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <... That's right. Hermann and her lackeys helped us.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I see.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Forget about that. Just what have you been doing here all this time, Meursault?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: And what is this place?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I am... currently in storage.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What does that even—
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: *sigh* Just as averse to explaining yourself as you were outside, even in this place.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Who are you people?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Back off. I found this material first. Finders keepers. It belongs to our store now.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: "Material"...? Um... Look, this dude is our... uh, "colleague." Can we have him back, please?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: "Colleague"... Hm. I've heard that word before. Is it a brand name?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Uh...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: From what we've seen of this place so far... I don't know if common sense is all that reliable in here.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: When you said he belongs to your store... does that mean you're gonna put him to work?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: No. We have more than enough staff for this shop. It's the material that's in shortage.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Material...? Oh, okay. I suppose you wanna, uh... borrow Meursault's uniform, then...?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: You strangers are impossible to communicate with. I'm at my wits' end here...
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: The employee gave us an exasperated look.
I said we're in a shortage of material. Material. What's so hard to understand about that?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Didn't you hear the announcement just now? The trend has changed again. A few seasons from now, there will be another thing that becomes the new trend. That's why we—and this shop—will always be in need of more material!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: I get that, I get that, but what the hell does that have to do with—
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Do any of you strangers have more common sense than this one? This one doesn't get a single word I'm saying!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: You're the one who—
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I think, Ishy... these people aren't about to hand Meur over just like that. We'll need to make a deal with them.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Sure, but a deal needs two-way communication, you know...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I get whatcha mean, Ishy. Ishy?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: I'm just sayin', I don't think asking more questions is our best shot at moving on.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: All right. Why don'tcha go ahead and tell me what you want in return for this, uh, "material"?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Now we're getting somewhere. All right, what do you want?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: It's a shame to lose such promising material... What to do, what to do...
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: ... All right, then. You can work off the material's value, and I'm willing to call it even. Consider it a part-time job. We're really swamped as it is, changing up the displays and order sheets to keep pace with the latest trends.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: S-sure... What kind of errand?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: There's an area nearby full of Mannequins.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: ... Mannequins?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Unable to restrain herself, Ishmael cut in once more, but quickly gave up when Rodion hurriedly sent a desperate look her way.
The problem is that those Mannequins are dressed in clothes that have fallen way, way behind the current fashion trend.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: What if customers coming here to shop see those hopelessly dated Mannequins and refuse to enter our store?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: R-right... That would be a real problem for the shop, wouldn't it...? Yeah... totally...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Rodya nodded vigorously, perhaps trying a little too hard to look sympathetic to the employee's plight.
Yes. Which means I want you to help the Mannequins to the exit.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: "Help them to the exit"? Okay, now I'm confused, too. Just what are we supposed to do?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The request is simple.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: We are to eliminate the entities they call "Mannequins."
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: You mean kill them?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: You are asking more questions than usual.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What do you expect? I can't understand half of what anyone here says.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I see.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: You see what?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I have realized that things here might appear inscrutable from your perspective.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: You should understand that, in this place, the word "common sense" may be received differently from its conventional usage.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Well? Are you helping those Mannequins to the exit or not?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Give us a sec~ Haha... We're just taking a quick look around your shop... These clothes are o-out of this world!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Oh, okay! Buy this, and I'll throw in that outfit as well. We're holding an end-of-season sale.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: So what's it gonna be? If we wanna save Meursault, we kill the things this person calls Mannequins—is that correct?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Correct.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Haven't you been browsing long enough? Don't you think you ought to buy something after that much window-shopping?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: <For now... let's head to where the Mannequins are.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Okay, then... we'll help them to the exit.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Good choice. You only need to help three Mannequins to the exit.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: <We'll be back, so stay in storage—I mean, wait for us here, Meursault.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... I must accompany you, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <What for?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Aw~ You're thinkin' we're not up to the task, aren'tcha?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: A question, Manager. It is likely that you have encountered entities they refer to as "Mannequins" on your way to this room. Did you try making physical contact with them?
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Uh... I'm not sure exactly what counts as a "Mannequin," but I haven't tried touching any of them just yet. Some didn't seem to perceive me at all, actually...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Indeed. Contact would have been impossible. I am likely the only person capable of direct intervention with the entities that exist in here.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: However, standing behind me in a line will allow for a limited degree of interactivity with the environment, though it will not be sufficient to engage these entities in battle.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Huh. And why is that...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Because this place belongs to the Symbolic, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Are ya sayin'... we cannot participate in any battles that take place in here?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: It will be possible in the Shadowed.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Symbolic, Shadowed... What are those?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: They are names for the constituent worlds of this department store.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Uh... That's not much of an answer, is it.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: A more thorough explanation than this would require a significant time investment.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <... Either way, we do need Meursault with us if we're going to make any real progress, right?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That is correct, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Then you should take the lead, Meursault.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <I'll tell you which way to go.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: It will be done.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: They need me to accompany them in order to fulfill the work you assigned to us. May I step away for a short while?
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Yeah, sure.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: <... Wait, we have Meursault now. What if we just split and never came back?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Fleeing would not prevent me from being placed in storage, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Okay... so you're saying runnin' away with you would cause trouble for us, right?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Correct.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Maybe this place has its own Laws—just like the Great Lake.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: *sigh* Let's do as Meursault says. I don't know why or how, but he seems to be well-acquainted with the department store.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Right. Sounds like a plan.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Can't wait around all day. Hurry up and make up your mind.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Well? Have you given it some thought?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Giving the clerk what they need is probably best if you require my service, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Since you're already on the job... hurry up, will you? This season could end any minute...
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: So this is... a "Mannequin?"
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Both this thing and what we saw earlier... they feel a lot like the things we call Distortions. What do you think, Dante?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <They do... I think they really are Distortions.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: No way... The trend changed again?
texts.speaker: Leather Glove

texts.text: What's in fashion now? I didn't hear the announcement.
texts.speaker: Leather Glove

texts.text: More importantly, how can you be walking around in hideous clothes like those? Aren't you even ashamed of yourselves? That couldn't possibly be the current trend!
texts.speaker: Leather Glove

texts.text: Stripes will return one day! Fashion always comes back around!
texts.speaker: Leather Glove

texts.text: Kergh... You dress in such repulsive rags... yet you call me outdated...?
texts.speaker: Leather Glove

texts.text: Next time... I'll make it. I'll be the one... to make it to the runway...
texts.speaker: Leather Glove

texts.text: So you managed to help them to the exit. Thanks to you, more customers can now access our shop.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Whew... We've got so much on our plates at the moment. We need to redesign and revamp the entire lineup, what with the trend changing.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Shame we're forced to part with this material, but that's that...
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: <color=#916e46>Your attention, please. The Houndstooth Season has officially ended. We are pleased to inform you that...</color>
Good grief! The trend changed again while I was wasting time shooting the breeze with you. Scram if you're not buying anything!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: So... you're not hurt anywhere, are you, Meur?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: There have been no violent altercations since I entered Sisyphe. I have sustained no injuries.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Why did they seize you in the first place?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: They believed I belonged to Le Kaki.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Le Kaki? What's that?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Questions and doubts everywhere—understandable, because Meursault showed no intention of explaining matters proactively, and even the words we thought we knew held completely different meanings to the entities in this place.
The customers of the department store can be classified into four principal groups, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The mainstream groups are called Le Noir and Le Rouge. Those belonging to neither are known as Le Kaki. Lastly, there are those who never reveal themselves, nor are they called upon by others.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Do these... "Kaki" people... often get kidnapped like that?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: It is inaccurate to label what happened to me as "kidnapping." The Kakis' existence is defined by the current's flow; therefore, they are sometimes used as tools or as materials for clothing production.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Most Kakis aim to purchase and wear the garments they desire. I possessed no such objective, which made it possible for them to use me as material.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I still don't get the full picture... So you need to have a fashion purpose here? Like... buying clothes, trying 'em on and stuff?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The people here... seemed interested in nothing but clothes.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: It is less a purpose than a raison d'être.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: With every answer breeding more questions, I had no choice but to cut in and ask the one fundamental subject someone had to ask.
<So, now that all's said and done, Meursault, could you tell us...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Where exactly we are?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Sisyphe...
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Yes, I know we're in Grand Magasin Sisyphe, and yes, it's a department store. But what I'm asking is...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Where in N Corp. is this building located? And what are all these people doing in here?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: What can we do to get out of this place?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: The barrage of questions were unrelenting, but Meursault kept his gaze trained on me without moving so much as an eyebrow.
There are more than a few questions, so I will address them individually.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Point one: This is not a physically constructed building, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Not physically constructed...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: My body currently lies unconscious inside a vat at the Sisyphe Tower, somewhere within N Corp.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The 12 bodies belonging to you and the other Sinners are likely inside the group Suicide Vending Machine you used.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Then... our minds have been moved here...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: And this is a virtual space inhabited by the minds of those sentenced to Sisyphe Penalty?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Correct.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I see. So that's why they made that disturbing experience an entry passage leading here...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Moving on, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Point two: Every person who enters the Grand Magasin Sisyphe is designated a "customer" who will do one of two things—manufacture clothing, or consume it.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Then I suppose everything we saw earlier counts as clothing too, right?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Correct.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: But I thought this place was supposed to be a Canned Experience factory. Imprisoning people's minds in a virtual space, making them manufacture clothing instead of cans—I mean, why do any of that?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: That is... not a question easily answered.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The question of how and why human beings exist does not admit any attempt at discovering an ultimate answer and, moreover, is a futile one to ask.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The questions of why the customers of Grand Magasin Sisyphe seek to purchase and wear clothing, and of why and through what process the department store came into existence... are likewise unfathomable subjects.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Sorry, why are we suddenly getting all existential? I was just asking what clothes and cans have to do with each other...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: It is an apt juxtaposition insofar as both are unanswerable, yet accepted by human perception.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What are you even—
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: All right, that's enough. I don't wanna keep going in circles over pointless gibberish. Any more of this and I'm gonna go crazy like the other wackos in here.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: So, let's summarize: this place looks real, but it's a virtual space where only our minds exist—like brains in a vat. Our bodies are all slumber partyin' nice and cozy inside that Suicide Vending Machine. The residents here are all nutjobs. Done. All cleared up.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: With that, our plan is simple: rescue Meur—we did that—find him in one piece—he is—yoink the Golden Bough on the rooftop, and get ourselves outta here. Everyone agree?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Laying it all out like that seemed to make things much simpler...
... and yet, having experienced enough ordeals throughout our journey, we knew all too well that it was easier said than done.
Point three:
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Please, no...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: There is no method by which an individual who enters Sisyphe...
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... may leave and return to the outside world at present.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Meursault delivered every grave word of the catastrophic verdict without a moment's hesitation.
<... Nothing we can even try? A loose Backdoor somewhere...? Maybe defeat a guard in here and leave...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Although it assumes the characteristics of a building, this is a symbolic space, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: It has no entrance or exit in the conventional sense.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Accordingly, even if we were to cross through some apparent passage leading to an "exit," it would only be a "representative" act—without resulting in our actual departure.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Y'know, it makes it even worse when ya say that awful conclusion so matter-of-factly...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: I did not speak matter-of-factly. I spoke the matter of fact.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Does that mean... there's no way out whatsoever for us?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Dante, can you not jinx us like that...?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: You and the others entered this place by means that cannot be described as conventional, Manager. An exit may exist in your case.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: However, that possibility does not guarantee that I can be removed from this place.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Ya sound like... you've been here before, Meur. Have you?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: This place is reserved for criminals sentenced to the Sisyphe Penalty. Residents who have not violated N Corp.'s laws cannot arrive here through ordinary means.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Then how do you know so much about it?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: ... I acquired the information while working for N Corp.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: It was difficult to imagine Meursault in an idle conversation with other people, with a cup in his hands.
But if nobody who enters can ever leave, how could anyone have told you—*sigh* never mind. Rodya's right. We're talking in circles now.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Anyway, it all comes down to us having to retrieve the Golden Bough, right? Even though there's no "proper" exit we can find.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Then... I suppose our only option is to climb toward the top. We found a way to sail through the Great Lake—we will find a way to navigate this place as well.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I considered for a moment whether it would be wise to point out that the ship had come equipped with a coordinates tracker to tell us where we were, but decided to bite my proverbial tongue. Deadpan truths are not always helpful.
Virtual or not, as the Manager of the team, there was only one thing I could ever say.
<Then let's keep moving. There should be stairs or something else that can take us to the next floor.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oh! You look like you've just got here, too! Right?

Thank goodness. I got sent here after being sentenced to the Sisyphe Penalty, but nobody would explain anything to me! All anyone says are riddles and nonsense when it comes to this place—and I mean people outside as well. The ones here? They even get angry and complain about me not having common sense!
And guess what, one person even asked if they could use me as material. Must be some kind of jargon they use in here.
So... when didya get here?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: That's exactly what I'm trying to figure out. There are no clocks here, and they have this weird way of counting days. Oh! Speaking of clocks—you've got one for a head! Could you tell me what time it is now? I know for sure it's been ages since my last meal, but somehow I don't feel hungry...
<Yup, that's the reaction of someone who just came from the outside world.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Whoa, are those uniforms? You must've belonged to a pretty serious Syndicate. Just what did you do that they decided to throw everyone in here as a package?
Hm, how should I put this... They charged us with "caring a lil' too much about a certain colleague of ours", if that makes sense?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: And you...? What did you do to receive the Penalty?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: There's this product my friends and I cooked up.
... I assume this "product" was illegal to manufacture in N Corp.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Whoa. How did you guess?
... I mean, it's obvious. Why else would they give you the Sisyphe Penalty?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Wow. You sound exactly like that prosecutor at my trial!

Everyone in the courtroom reprimanded me so hard once my trial began. They said something about how I was sowing confusion and unrest among the residents of N Corp. by distributing products like that...
What exactly did you make?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Counterfeit Canned Experience. Oh, I'm the one who designed the label, by the way—I've been quite an artist since I was little. Laura was in charge of the contents. It's easy stuff. All you need is some flour, chalk dust, and a pinch of powdered milk. The ratio of the ingredients is where you need to be careful.
Counterfeit Canned Experience...? That's a thing?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Huh? Why wouldn't it be? I mean, you only need to make it look the same. Believe me, there are plenty of people in the Backstreets who make a living by making fake Canned Experiences. People can't get enough of anything labeled "experience," after all.
Anyway, this is the first time I've experienced the Sisyphe Penalty. Maybe they'll let me out sooner if I can post bail. Bernard said he'd try to raise the money from selling the fake cans.
Right... And what happened to your face...? Did they hurt you or something?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Oh, I got this from a fire that broke out in the orphanage I grew up in. I couldn't get proper treatment in time what with being an urchin and all, and... well. Bernard has it worse—he's left with a permanent limp. Even worse for Laura. Breathing in smoke really messed up her lungs, so she can't run for too long. Say goodbye to ever working in a Nest with scars like these, right?
But hey, at least this prison's pretty snazzy. And I've never seen or heard of a prison where they let you wander around without locking you up in a cell.
The name's Dubois, by the way. People also call me "Scar D."
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: This guy...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: He has no idea what is happening. Just like us a little while ago...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I don't know, I... kinda feel bad for him...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: And, uh... he's kinda neurotic, too, jumping from one subject to the other.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: By the way... If this is a prison, where are the guards...? Shouldn't jails have wardens or something?
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Who knows...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Oh, and... Do you happen to know how to get upstairs? There might be a phone booth or something up there on the upper floors. I need to call my friends.
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: We're looking for a way up too.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Oh, I see... Okay. I'll let you know if I manage to find one.
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: I'll be keeping an eye out for any staircases or elevators leading up!
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: [미사용] 이제 퀘스트는 없어
texts.speaker: 뉴비1 npc

texts.text: This employee here isn't so eager to greet us.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Is that... normal?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Vendors of Le Noir establishments are not compelled to initiate provider-client engagement.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Welp, then let's not bother 'em and move on? Sounds like a win-win.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: We can almost feel his guarded stare against our skin. If he's not about to stop us from browsing, why is he watching us like a hawk...?
It looks something like a suit... only cut from a far more classy design.
Huh. That's actually a lot nicer than I expected. So chic!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: ... Let's look around some more.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Ooh, don'tcha think this one's made for Dante?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <Y-you think so?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ya bet! That fit is practically beggin' for ya. And we've got those eyeballs from earlier—why not treat yourself?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Hang on. It's the only kind of currency they'll accept around here. We should set our priorities right before we splash cash like—
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Don't worry, Ishmael. We can't afford it anyway.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We can't?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Eeep... 450 eyeballs? What a ripoff!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Or maybe we're just too broke.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Unlike the Casualwear Hall, everything here has the same sort of look.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: These garments do not submit to passing trends.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The collections sold by Contemporary labels of Le Noir and Le Rouge each maintain a deliberate visual consistency, according to the aesthetic doctrine of their respective factions.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <But if they keep making the same kinds of clothes... won't fashion leave them behind? Trends change every 5 minutes in this place.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That is—
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: When a designer's name carries enough weight, ya don't chase trends. Trends chase ya instead.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Slap a famous label and a ridiculous price on something this fancy, and people will line up before ya lift a finger.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: No need to run yourself ragged.. to keep up with every little craze.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The entire outfit fits neatly into view.
<Come to think of it, almost everything on display in this department store is clothing. Wonder what their production line looks like.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Grand Magasin Sisyphe offers various opportunities to procure a sundry of material and attachments, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Well... Outside, I think they get the mats from domesticated animals or plants...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: That, or use synthetic fiber for weaving.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Though the label upon each material differ from those of the outside,
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: the basic manufacturing principles remain the same: butcher the source and use the raw material for production.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The "raw material" being...?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Being the clientele. This means they purchase and wear clothing, but may also become clothing themselves.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Right... So how big is Sisyphe's "clientele"? The customers trapped in this place?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Approximately 300 million.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Pretty sure I misheard that.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: You did not. There is no discharge date for the Sisyphe Penalty, and those who enter remain permanently. Its population is theoretically on an infinite upward trend.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>Heed ye, for again I proclaim this day. Blessed be the hall of our rest with eternal preservation.</color>

<color=#7d7d7d>Yet even today, ye do naught as the hideous and the wicked ceaselessly tear out the Golden from its walls and take its aureate light for themselves. How long will ye forgive your own craven spirits and feebly accept the end of days?</color>
I shall heed your command, Lord. Apostates who dare plunder the Golden Resin shall—
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: I see among our clientele... those who gladly bask in the tarnished glow of sacrilege.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Why is he looking at us...? Hey, we were just shopping and minding our own business!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The employee is speaking to the Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Me? What? Why?!>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: That the forces of Le Rouge would seek to foment disorder and profane the sacred domain... Answer, what is this brazen attempt to null the ancient truce?
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: You listen here, Buddy. I don't even know what this funny "Rouge" business is, 'kay? We're nobodies, we're not in any forces of whatever, and we don't want any trouble!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Ah, then you claim to be Kakis? You, who strut through our store flaunting those irreverent trinkets on your face? Do you expect us to believe you?
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: If I were to hazard a guess... I'd say the "blasphemous trinkets" are referring to Dante's clock hands...?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Okay... So what's that got to do with us?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: It is likely due to the guiding tenets of the Le Noir faction.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I was informed that they consider the eternal preservation of this department store to be their appointed mission.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text:
<color=#7d7d7d>Thou shalt not suffer those who would scrape out the Golden.
Thou shalt cleanse our domain of apostasy.</color>

I shall grant them no mercy... I shall reclaim that radiant resin with my own hands and shore up the fading light of this sanctuary... Yes—your voice reaches me. As the hand of the will that is Le Noir, I shall make my stand here and...!
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text:
<color=#7d7d7d>Thou shalt banish the apostates...
Thou shalt preserve the Golden hue...
Thou art hallow'd with the divine duty to shade the profane light, O keeper of eternal rest...</color>
W-wait... Lower your weapons, please...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Your aureate traces are... while similar, quite unlike the Golden Resin we must preserve.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Yeah, well, why didn't you listen when we said as much? Could've avoided this whole mess...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Ishmael took a threatening stride toward the employee, who quickly shrank back.

Oh! I understand... Your voice resounds within me once more! These are true strangers, innocent of our ways—customers drawn here by the worth of our brand, and nothing more. I shall receive them anew.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Forgive my affront, dear customers. The golden light that hangs over you much resembles the blessed Golden Resin we must preserve.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: We haven't met too many people who could pick up the Golden Bough's presence like you did... How'd ya do it?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Every one of us feels that golden pulse... and thirsts for it.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Our guiding light... The golden gleam that weaves us into our desired forms...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: We desire it too, that brilliance. But unlike the Rouges who surrendered to their base urges, we Noirs are the eternally sworn guards of the blessed grain.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: As you have doubtless noticed... The walls are riddled with the hideous bite marks left by those blasphemous red ones.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Grain of the Golden Resin, indeed... But those Rouge savages are busy shoveling that very essence of the stalwart bastion into their gullets...!
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Okay, so... just what is the "Golden Resin"?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Does this have anything to do with the Golden Boughs?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... I think he's talking about these... patches.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Rodya pointed at one of the walls sparsely covered in patches of faded resin.
So they're the "Golden Resin," huh...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: The time was nine arboreal Seasons ago—when the Age of Ruin descended upon Grand Magasin Sisyphe in the form of cataclysmic cracks forming upon its walls.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Then, mere moments before doom took us, salvation arrived in a form that couldn't be anything else but divine—brilliant resin of gold, materializing in the cracks that would have been our ruin, patching them back to wholeness. Are we not to praise and worship this providence? Alas... The Rouges fail to comprehend the unequivocal logic in this veneration, and instead elect to flay the walls... Preposterous.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Though a precarious truce between the two factions is in place... None fail to see the truth that is plainly before them: this peace is but a momentary lull, nothing more.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Then... only then... shall my mind be opened to the true "Voice," beyond the broadcast.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: ...? What was all that fuss about voices earlier, then?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Uh...! Right, indeed... I do hear the "Voice..." What I meant to say is that my mind shall be opened further so that I may hear it more frequently...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Anyways... If ya know a way upstairs, care to let us in on the secret?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Ah, so you are customers who seek to reach the Customer Service Center, I see...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: To rise is to gain prestige, and to be prestigious is to spend and consume until your expenditure befits the status they demand.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Though I am bound to my post, to remain in this establishment and attend to its customers...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: ... perhaps you may be able to ascend in my stead and relay the account of my eternal fidelity toward the Golden Resin...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Gotcha. So if we want to go upstairs, we're gonna need to spend some cash. One more question, if you wouldn't mind—how exactly do we make money around here?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: ... Money?
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: The lingo for money here seems to be "eyeballs"... Right?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Oh... You strangers truly possess a determination unlike any other.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Then I shall reveal the means by which eyeballs may be won. Take them from the Mannequins. They seek every opportunity to exhibit themselves without end; if you apply yourselves diligently, you will gather all the eyeballs you require.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: And another thing—pray, be constantly vigilant beyond this point, for you will be entering the territory of the Rouges. The vulgar, heathen fiends cannot even drape a bolt of fabric properly, so they rend our Golden Resin and stitch it back together in whatever blasphemous shape that pleases them...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: ... The Rouges... All right. Will keep that in mind.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: If there isn't anything else, brave strangers, I am honored to inform you that this establishment is now open to your perusal.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: I think we've looked at pretty much everything they have to offer here.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <Those are some pretty bizarre things they're selling here... Do all shops here have such a weird inventory?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Well, let's head to the other store up ahead and find out.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Oh... How regrettable. We carry nothing suitable for Strangers of your... sensibilities. Return once you've cultivated some understanding of fashion—and raised your rank, too.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: And how do we raise that?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: There is but one way to raise one's standing in a department store, is there not?
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: ... Spend money. Lots of it.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Precisely. Then until we meet again, Strangers of truly... arresting fashion.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Welcome, dear customers—
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Ah... Do I spy a true connoisseur of fashion? A style much like our own... sophisticated... elegant... and that command of color—exquisite.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Hah! See? Someone gets it.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The compliment was directed at the Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Huh... Guess I'm pretty "hip" here, as they say?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Congrats, I guess...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: You appear to possess a respectable eye for fashion, so perhaps I can offer an expert's advice on shopping...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: The soul of our label is liberation—strangling liberation, to be exact. You passed through the Noirs' store, yes? All those steel pins hammered through the fabric are a hypocritical pantomime of restraint—the philosophy of Le Rouge differs at its very root.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: If I may direct your attention... here, do you see the smooth, natural give of the material? You won't see that from any production technique other than toothed—yes, it is quite literal—loopwheeling technique. The hide spills downward, completing a silhouette at once effortless and sublime.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Ah! And I would be remiss not to share that this includes 0.3 ounces of Golden Hide blended into the material. Simply feel it in your hands—ah, it has such a wonderful luster that practically gleams along the surface, doesn't it? Doesn't it?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: I couldn't help but notice that she was hungrily licking her lips throughout the rant.
It-it does...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Ah, do pardon me... I got carried away, didn't I?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: The truth is, I am the designer of this label.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Gosh, I could go on for hours about all the troubles I had to overcome to have this tiny corner of the department store to myself. It's no easy task launching a designer label at Sisyphe, you know.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Well... at least she seems to fall into the friendly camp.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Is there a particular silhouette you're after? If you like, I can select a line from my collection that will articulate your physique to perfection.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: We're... trying to find our way upstairs, actually.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: The upper floors...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Ah, I knew it... You're more interested in the Luxury brands too, aren't you?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: But I assure you, the quality standards and the classique air of my designs are not so far behind those of Luxury brands...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Yes, of course, the allure of Luxury brands is undeniable. There once was a time when even I devoted myself to collecting eyeballs like a thing possessed, all for the chance of witnessing the Luxury Hall...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: No, we're just...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I know a Rouge who used to work here before they were allowed to join the Luxury Hall. I don't want to badmouth, but I do take umbrage with how they approved somebody who is so clearly my inferior in patterning and design. And to think this "Luxury designer" learned their craft under my tutelage as a greenhorn, can you believe it?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Until... listen, this is where it gets really ridiculous...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: ... they used their teeth to line each and every one of their items with exactly 76 tooth marks along the necklines and hems. Whatever it was that the customers saw, the general reception claimed it cast a "deconstructive silhouette," and practically emptied their shelves.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Eh, I wouldn't attribute that to their skill when it ultimately amounts to a fluke... My designs are far more sophisticated than theirs, not to mention incomparably elegant.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: I deserve to be recognized as a Luxury house, too. A couture label of my own! But just what must I do to—
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: ... Oh, I've a brilliant inspiration.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Would you mind grabbing me a needle from the Exhibiting Mannequins?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Find me a sizable one, and I'll try to make it worth your while.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: That Mannequin seemed tougher than the others... Ya think it's this golden needle?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Have you brought me the needle?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Yeah, here's your needle. So... care to explain how this is your key to joining the Luxury brands?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: It's just something that's struck me all of a sudden. Does my brand need strong heritage to enter the world of high fashion? No. Technical perfection? Clearly not. Rare, high-grade materials? Not at all...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: But I've been so obsessed with meeting those arbitrary conditions that I've trapped myself in this glorified glass jar of a lobby.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Yes, a signature piece... What I lacked was the signature piece—do you understand what I'm getting at?—the singular idea that would seize every customer's eye just from a quick glance...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: She took the massive needle from us, raised it to her eye level... then began rapidly stabbing her own skin with it.
If I give it a nice pattern... like so... I can easily create a sense of three-dimensionality. Just wait until you see the material swell up evenly across the board.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Ohh, I can't wait to feel each hole in the pattern fill up with soft, juicy pus! It'll result in such a supple touch... How's that? It'll fit right in among the masterpieces of the Luxury Hall on the upper floors, won't it? won't it?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: S-sure it would, I think...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Is that all you've got to say? You have an eye for beauty—use it! Appreciate what you see!
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: ... 21 punctures along the horizontal axis and 21 along the vertical, intersecting at uniform intervals. That would produce the greatest density.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Of course... A hybrid construction of the quilting process and embossed design formed into diamond shapes.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Anyway, we helped you out, as promised. I think it's about time you held up your end of the deal and told us how to get ourselves upstairs.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Oh, that? You simply need to build up your Prestige Tier. At your current level, of course, you should probably start your shopping journey down at the Casualwear Hall...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: ... But since you've been tremendously helpful in my fashion ventures, I'll make a special exception for you and allow purchase from my brand.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: <No freebies after all, huh.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Mark my words: the next time we meet... perhaps you will see me in the Luxury Hall, showcasing my piece—or shall I say, myself—in an exalted window display. Ahh... What bliss...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Look at me, wasting my time chattering away when the deadline for the next collection is fast approaching... Excuse me while I finish embossing the shoulder seam...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: In the meantime, feel free to browse my designer collection! No item is off limits for purchase...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: What a... bizarre assortment of products.
Oh, hello again! I found the escalator, but it won't run.
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Really? That's weird, why wouldn't it...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Wait, it's running now that you're here! You must've found a way to unlock your way onto the upper floor!
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Well, we did a lil' shopping... some grunt work... some more grunt work...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Can I tag along? I promise I'll repay you guys as soon as I find a way to make some money myself.
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Don't see what the harm could be... Hop right on, I guess?
